title: Synthetic Theory Note: Distributed Expertise and Shared Visibility
citation: Demonstration source created for this prototype; not a published theory article.

passages.text: When interdependent units can see one another's current capacities, they can identify relevant expertise and coordinate laterally without waiting for a central actor to discover available resources.
Shared visibility supports rapid provisional commitments when actions can be revised and when the displayed information is trusted.
Visibility alone does not remove formal authority. A consequential veto or unreliable information can return initiative to the center and slow the process.
